Question 1 of 20, Level 1

1MCQCBSE 2024 (65/1/3) Q71 mark
A relation RRR defined on a set of human beings as R={(x,y):x is 5 cm shorter than y}R = \{(x, y) : x \text{ is 5 cm shorter than } y\}R={(x,y):x is 5 cm shorter than y} is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Reflexive: (a,a)∈R(a,a) \in R(a,a)∈R; symmetric: (a,b)∈R⇒(b,a)∈R(a,b) \in R \Rightarrow (b,a) \in R(a,b)∈R⇒(b,a)∈R; transitive: (a,b),(b,c)∈R⇒(a,c)∈R(a,b), (b,c) \in R \Rightarrow (a,c) \in R(a,b),(b,c)∈R⇒(a,c)∈R.

  1. 1

    Reflexive? Nobody is 5 cm shorter than himself.

    (x,x)∉R(x, x) \notin R(x,x)∈/R
  2. 2

    Symmetric? If xxx is 5 cm shorter than yyy, then yyy is 5 cm taller.

    (x,y)∈R  ⇒  (y,x)∉R(x, y) \in R \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \notin R(x,y)∈R⇒(y,x)∈/R(x,y)∈R  ⇒  (y,x)∉R\displaystyle (x, y) \in R \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \notin R(x,y)∈R⇒(y,x)∈/R
  3. 3

    Transitive? Let xxx be 5 cm shorter than yyy, and yyy than zzz.

    x is 10 cm shorter than z  ⇒  (x,z)∉Rx \text{ is 10 cm shorter than } z \;\Rightarrow\; (x, z) \notin Rx is 10 cm shorter than z⇒(x,z)∈/Rx is 10 cm shorter than z  ⇒  (x,z)∉R\displaystyle x \text{ is 10 cm shorter than } z \;\Rightarrow\; (x, z) \notin Rx is 10 cm shorter than z⇒(x,z)∈/R
    1
  4. 4

    RRR has none of the three properties. Option (D).

Answer(D) neither transitive, nor symmetric, nor reflexive

Watch out Treating it like ‘shorter than’, which is transitive — ‘exactly 5 cm shorter’ is not.

Assertion (A): The relation R={(x,y):(x+y) is a prime number and x,y∈N}R = \{(x, y) : (x + y) \text{ is a prime number and } x, y \in \mathbb{N}\}R={(x,y):(x+y) is a prime number and x,y∈N} is not a reflexive relation. Reason (R): The number 2n2n2n is composite for all natural numbers nnn.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea (x,x)∈R(x, x) \in R(x,x)∈R needs x+x=2xx + x = 2xx+x=2x to be prime.

  1. 1

    Check A: take x=2x = 2x=2.

    2+2=4 is not prime  ⇒  (2,2)∉R2 + 2 = 4 \text{ is not prime} \;\Rightarrow\; (2, 2) \notin R2+2=4 is not prime⇒(2,2)∈/R2+2=4 is not prime  ⇒  (2,2)∉R\displaystyle 2 + 2 = 4 \text{ is not prime} \;\Rightarrow\; (2, 2) \notin R2+2=4 is not prime⇒(2,2)∈/R

    so RRR is not reflexive: A is true

  2. 2

    Check R: take n=1n = 1n=1.

    2n=2, which is prime, not composite2n = 2, \text{ which is prime, not composite}2n=2, which is prime, not composite2n=2, which is prime, not composite\displaystyle 2n = 2, \text{ which is prime, not composite}2n=2, which is prime, not composite

    so R is false

    1
  3. 3

    A false statement cannot explain A.

  4. 4

    A is true, R is false. Option (C).

Answer(C) A is true, but R is false

Watch out Forgetting n=1n = 1n=1: then 2n=22n = 22n=2 is prime, so R fails.

A function fff is defined from R→R\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}R→R as f(x)=ax+bf(x) = ax + bf(x)=ax+b, such that f(1)=1f(1) = 1f(1)=1 and f(2)=3f(2) = 3f(2)=3. Find function f(x)f(x)f(x). Hence, check whether function f(x)f(x)f(x) is one-one and onto or not.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Onto: for every yyy in the codomain, solve f(x)=yf(x) = yf(x)=y and check xxx lies in the domain.

  1. 1

    Use the given values.

    f(1)=a+b=1,f(2)=2a+b=3f(1) = a + b = 1, \qquad f(2) = 2a + b = 3f(1)=a+b=1,f(2)=2a+b=3f(1)=a+b=1,f(2)=2a+b=3\displaystyle f(1) = a + b = 1, \qquad f(2) = 2a + b = 3f(1)=a+b=1,f(2)=2a+b=3
  2. 2

    Subtract to get aaa, then find bbb.

    a=2, b=−1  ⇒  f(x)=2x−1a = 2, \ b = -1 \;\Rightarrow\; f(x) = 2x - 1a=2, b=−1⇒f(x)=2x−1a=2, b=−1  ⇒  f(x)=2x−1\displaystyle a = 2, \ b = -1 \;\Rightarrow\; f(x) = 2x - 1a=2, b=−1⇒f(x)=2x−1
    ½
  3. 3

    One-one: let f(x1)=f(x2)f(x_1) = f(x_2)f(x1​)=f(x2​).

    2x1−1=2x2−1  ⇒  x1=x22x_1 - 1 = 2x_2 - 1 \;\Rightarrow\; x_1 = x_22x1​−1=2x2​−1⇒x1​=x2​2x1−1=2x2−1  ⇒  x1=x2\displaystyle 2x_1 - 1 = 2x_2 - 1 \;\Rightarrow\; x_1 = x_22x1​−1=2x2​−1⇒x1​=x2​
    ½
  4. 4

    Onto: let y∈Ry \in \mathbb{R}y∈R and solve f(x)=yf(x) = yf(x)=y.

    2x−1=y  ⇒  x=y+12∈R2x - 1 = y \;\Rightarrow\; x = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} \in \mathbb{R}2x−1=y⇒x=2y+1​∈R2x−1=y  ⇒  x=y+12∈R\displaystyle 2x - 1 = y \;\Rightarrow\; x = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} \in \mathbb{R}2x−1=y⇒x=2y+1​∈R
    ½
  5. 5

    Check the pre-image.

    f(y+12)=(y+1)−1=yf\left(\dfrac{y + 1}{2}\right) = (y + 1) - 1 = yf(2y+1​)=(y+1)−1=yf(y+12)=(y+1)−1=y\displaystyle f\left(\dfrac{y + 1}{2}\right) = (y + 1) - 1 = yf(2y+1​)=(y+1)−1=y
    ½
  6. 6

    Hence f(x)=2x−1f(x) = 2x - 1f(x)=2x−1 is both one-one and onto.

Answerf(x)=2x−1\displaystyle f(x) = 2x - 1f(x)=2x−1; it is both one-one and onto.

Watch out Finding x=y+12x = \dfrac{y+1}{2}x=2y+1​ but not showing f(x)=yf(x) = yf(x)=y for it.

Question 6Question 8

Question 8 of 20, Level 2

8Short answerPYQ-style2 marks
Show that the relation RRR on the set Z\mathbb{Z}Z of integers, given by R={(a,b):2a+3b is divisible by 5}R = \{(a, b) : 2a + 3b \text{ is divisible by } 5\}R={(a,b):2a+3b is divisible by 5}, is an equivalence relation.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea An equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

  1. 1

    Reflexive: put b=ab = ab=a.

    2a+3a=5a, divisible by 5  ⇒  (a,a)∈R2a + 3a = 5a, \text{ divisible by } 5 \;\Rightarrow\; (a, a) \in R2a+3a=5a, divisible by 5⇒(a,a)∈R2a+3a=5a, divisible by 5  ⇒  (a,a)∈R\displaystyle 2a + 3a = 5a, \text{ divisible by } 5 \;\Rightarrow\; (a, a) \in R2a+3a=5a, divisible by 5⇒(a,a)∈R
    ½
  2. 2

    Symmetric: let (a,b)∈R(a, b) \in R(a,b)∈R, so 2a+3b=5k2a + 3b = 5k2a+3b=5k.

    2b+3a=5(a+b)−(2a+3b)=5(a+b−k)2b + 3a = 5(a + b) - (2a + 3b) = 5(a + b - k)2b+3a=5(a+b)−(2a+3b)=5(a+b−k)2b+3a=5(a+b)−(2a+3b)=5(a+b−k)\displaystyle 2b + 3a = 5(a + b) - (2a + 3b) = 5(a + b - k)2b+3a=5(a+b)−(2a+3b)=5(a+b−k)
    ½
  3. 3

    So 555 divides 2b+3a2b + 3a2b+3a, i.e. (b,a)∈R(b, a) \in R(b,a)∈R.

  4. 4

    Transitive: let (a,b),(b,c)∈R(a, b), (b, c) \in R(a,b),(b,c)∈R and add the two conditions.

    (2a+3b)+(2b+3c)=5k+5m  ⇒  2a+5b+3c=5(k+m)(2a + 3b) + (2b + 3c) = 5k + 5m \;\Rightarrow\; 2a + 5b + 3c = 5(k + m)(2a+3b)+(2b+3c)=5k+5m⇒2a+5b+3c=5(k+m)(2a+3b)+(2b+3c)=5k+5m  ⇒  2a+5b+3c=5(k+m)\displaystyle (2a + 3b) + (2b + 3c) = 5k + 5m \;\Rightarrow\; 2a + 5b + 3c = 5(k + m)(2a+3b)+(2b+3c)=5k+5m⇒2a+5b+3c=5(k+m)
  5. 5

    Rearrange.

    2a+3c=5(k+m−b)  ⇒  (a,c)∈R2a + 3c = 5(k + m - b) \;\Rightarrow\; (a, c) \in R2a+3c=5(k+m−b)⇒(a,c)∈R2a+3c=5(k+m−b)  ⇒  (a,c)∈R\displaystyle 2a + 3c = 5(k + m - b) \;\Rightarrow\; (a, c) \in R2a+3c=5(k+m−b)⇒(a,c)∈R
    ½
  6. 6

    Hence RRR is an equivalence relation.

    ½
AnswerR\displaystyle RR is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation.

Watch out Writing 2b+3a=2a+3b2b + 3a = 2a + 3b2b+3a=2a+3b — false in general; use 5(a+b)5(a + b)5(a+b) minus the given sum.

Question 7Question 9

9Short answerCBSE 2023 (65/1/1) Q323 marks
A relation RRR is defined on the set of real numbers R\mathbb{R}R as R={(x,y):x⋅y is an irrational number}R = \{(x, y) : x \cdot y \text{ is an irrational number}\}R={(x,y):x⋅y is an irrational number}. Check whether RRR is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea To prove a property, argue for all elements; to disprove it, one counter-example is enough.

  1. 1

    Reflexive? Take x=1x = 1x=1.

    1⋅1=1, rational  ⇒  (1,1)∉R1 \cdot 1 = 1, \text{ rational} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, 1) \notin R1⋅1=1, rational⇒(1,1)∈/R1⋅1=1, rational  ⇒  (1,1)∉R\displaystyle 1 \cdot 1 = 1, \text{ rational} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, 1) \notin R1⋅1=1, rational⇒(1,1)∈/R

    so RRR is not reflexive

    1
  2. 2

    Symmetric: let (x,y)∈R(x, y) \in R(x,y)∈R.

    x⋅y irrational  ⇒  y⋅x=x⋅y irrational  ⇒  (y,x)∈Rx \cdot y \text{ irrational} \;\Rightarrow\; y \cdot x = x \cdot y \text{ irrational} \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \in Rx⋅y irrational⇒y⋅x=x⋅y irrational⇒(y,x)∈Rx⋅y irrational  ⇒  y⋅x=x⋅y irrational  ⇒  (y,x)∈R\displaystyle x \cdot y \text{ irrational} \;\Rightarrow\; y \cdot x = x \cdot y \text{ irrational} \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \in Rx⋅y irrational⇒y⋅x=x⋅y irrational⇒(y,x)∈R

    multiplication of real numbers is commutative

    1
  3. 3

    Transitive? Take x=1x = 1x=1, y=2y = \sqrt{2}y=2​, z=2z = 2z=2.

    1⋅2=2,2⋅2=22(both irrational)1 \cdot \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}, \quad \sqrt{2} \cdot 2 = 2\sqrt{2} \quad (\text{both irrational})1⋅2​=2​,2​⋅2=22​(both irrational)1⋅2=2,2⋅2=22(both irrational)\displaystyle 1 \cdot \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2}, \quad \sqrt{2} \cdot 2 = 2\sqrt{2} \quad (\text{both irrational})1⋅2​=2​,2​⋅2=22​(both irrational)
  4. 4

    So (1,2)∈R(1, \sqrt{2}) \in R(1,2​)∈R and (2,2)∈R(\sqrt{2}, 2) \in R(2​,2)∈R. But:

    1⋅2=2, rational  ⇒  (1,2)∉R1 \cdot 2 = 2, \text{ rational} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, 2) \notin R1⋅2=2, rational⇒(1,2)∈/R1⋅2=2, rational  ⇒  (1,2)∉R\displaystyle 1 \cdot 2 = 2, \text{ rational} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, 2) \notin R1⋅2=2, rational⇒(1,2)∈/R
    1
  5. 5

    Hence RRR is symmetric, but neither reflexive nor transitive.

AnswerR\displaystyle RR is symmetric, but neither reflexive nor transitive.

Watch out Trying to prove transitivity in general — pick a counter-example with a common middle term.

    x+x=2x, divisible by 2  ⇒  (x,x)∈Rx + x = 2x, \text{ divisible by } 2 \;\Rightarrow\; (x, x) \in Rx+x=2x, divisible by 2⇒(x,x)∈Rx+x=2x, divisible by 2  ⇒  (x,x)∈R\displaystyle x + x = 2x, \text{ divisible by } 2 \;\Rightarrow\; (x, x) \in Rx+x=2x, divisible by 2⇒(x,x)∈R

    y+x=x+y=2k  ⇒  (y,x)∈Ry + x = x + y = 2k \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \in Ry+x=x+y=2k⇒(y,x)∈Ry+x=x+y=2k  ⇒  (y,x)∈R\displaystyle y + x = x + y = 2k \;\Rightarrow\; (y, x) \in Ry+x=x+y=2k⇒(y,x)∈R

    (x+y)+(y+z)=2k+2m  ⇒  x+2y+z=2(k+m)(x + y) + (y + z) = 2k + 2m \;\Rightarrow\; x + 2y + z = 2(k + m)(x+y)+(y+z)=2k+2m⇒x+2y+z=2(k+m)(x+y)+(y+z)=2k+2m  ⇒  x+2y+z=2(k+m)\displaystyle (x + y) + (y + z) = 2k + 2m \;\Rightarrow\; x + 2y + z = 2(k + m)(x+y)+(y+z)=2k+2m⇒x+2y+z=2(k+m)

Case Study: A city’s traffic management department is planning to optimize traffic flow by analyzing the connectivity between various traffic signals. The city has five major spots labelled A,B,C,DA, B, C, DA,B,C,D and EEE. The department has collected the following data regarding one-way traffic flow between spots: traffic flows from AAA to BBB, AAA to CCC and AAA to DDD; from BBB to CCC and BBB to EEE; from CCC to EEE; from DDD to EEE and DDD to CCC. The department wants to represent and analyze this data using relations and functions, taking (X,Y)∈R(X, Y) \in R(X,Y)∈R when traffic flows from XXX to YYY, on the set S={A,B,C,D,E}S = \{A, B, C, D, E\}S={A,B,C,D,E}.
